findings.governingReading: an exertive “Ei!” as Sakura thrusts out her hand
findings.explanation: mirror moon invents a spoken hand choice that the next page immediately contradicts when Sakura is shown to have played paper.

findings.highlight: cooking dinner seems like a favorite pastime for us
findings.evidenceJa: 夕食の支度は娯楽の一つであるらしい
findings.governingReading: dinner preparation seems to be one of the amusements in this household
findings.explanation: The qualified comic observation becomes a stronger preference ranking.

findings.governingReading: when both of us are free
findings.explanation: Available time is recast as dissatisfaction, changing the tone of the domestic ritual.

findings.highlight: Sakura and I are the only ones here
findings.evidenceJa: 桜は上機嫌で台所に立っている
findings.governingReading: Sakura is in the kitchen in high spirits
findings.explanation: The sentence drops Sakura’s visibly happy mood, which motivates Shirou’s watching and the scene’s domestic warmth.

findings.highlight: Am I watching her because I have nothing to do?
findings.evidenceJa: それとも、無意識に目が追ってしまうのか
findings.governingReading: or are my eyes unconsciously following her
findings.explanation: Shirou’s alternative explanation—unconscious attraction—is removed, leaving only idleness.
The first physical detail in Shirou’s attentive inventory is reduced.

findings.highlight: She holds the heavy kitchen knife
findings.evidenceJa: 重そうながらもしっかりと包丁を持って
findings.governingReading: although it looks heavy for her, she grips the knife firmly
findings.explanation: Sakura’s effort and secure handling become a simple property of the knife.

findings.highlight: She cuts it with a yell
findings.evidenceJa: えい、と気合をこめて入刀する
findings.governingReading: with an “ei,” she puts her spirit into the first cut
findings.explanation: A small effort sound and bracing gesture are inflated into yelling.

findings.highlight: Sakura tenses up every times she starts to cut something
findings.evidenceJa: 桜はどんな物でもそんなふうに緊張して
findings.governingReading: Sakura tenses up that way whenever she begins cutting anything
findings.explanation: The English uses an ungrammatical plural in an adverbial phrase.

findings.highlight: I suddenly realize how hard this life is to obtain
findings.evidenceJa: それが得がたいものなのだと気がついた
findings.governingReading: I suddenly realize that this is something precious and difficult to come by
findings.explanation: The English preserves the idea but renders an ordinary life as an object one “obtains,” obscuring the realization’s natural emotional force.
Both the body and the written growth layer disappear, weakening the distinction between recent physical awareness and older attachment.

findings.highlight: I was confused by her femininity
findings.evidenceJa: 女の子としての桜に動揺して、参り始めている
findings.governingReading: he has been shaken by Sakura as a girl and has begun to be overcome or fall for her
findings.explanation: The English reduces an intensifying romantic surrender to cognitive confusion.

findings.highlight: If I’m confused, it started long before that
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が参っているとしたら、それはもっと前からだ
findings.governingReading: if she has me beaten or undone, it began much earlier
findings.explanation: The corrective realization about the depth and duration of Shirou’s attachment repeats the mistranslation as longstanding confusion.
The sound’s soft quality, which anchors the following reflection on ordinary tenderness, is omitted.

findings.highlight: I pour myself a third cup of tea
findings.evidenceJa: ぼんやりとした頭で三杯目のお茶を淹れて
findings.governingReading: with his head pleasantly hazy, he pours a third cup of tea
findings.explanation: The altered, dreamy state that prompts the alcohol fancy is removed.
